title: Master! Yes! Stability and Clarity
speaker: Nomon Tim Burnett
summary: Nomon Tim Burnett invites participants to approach their retreat with an open heart and mind, focusing on cultivating love, confidence, and mindfulness rather than trying to achieve a specific outcome or expectation. This practice is seen as a way to repay their parents for all that they've given them, not through external actions but through the development of virtue and discernment from within. By embracing the ordinary moments of life as opportunities for practice and connection with others, we can cultivate generosity, love, and kindness in our minds and hearts.

Which two?
Your mother and father.

So maybe that's part of why we're here this week, to repay our parents through practice, through practicing, because there's really no such thing as practice actually.

*We are already exactly peaceful and harmonious.

*This is the root.

This is to be a human being.

For 2,500 years, the Buddha has been teaching us that we are Buddha, that we lack nothing, and we already have the highest enlightenment.
Still we do not completely understand, and even though we understand, it has not settled down in our hearts.

And that seems like it's true enough, it does calm us down and does help us go on,

but I don't think we ever would have imagined the dimensions of what happens or what seems to happen. Of course, it can't really quite be described in words, but this way that the heart opens, this way that listening to the birds and feeling our breath and watching each other move around as we do our thing would somehow enable us to gradually and steadily, with a few fits and starts, kind of untwist and untangle and open our hearts to each other and to the world. over time it softens us up and we remember that life is about love. Why? Well, the Buddha was asked many questions, some of which are written down in thousands and thousands of pages, some of the questions he was asked, and I bet he was asked many more questions than that.
